newsitem.title: CHINA: China job market seen facing growing pressure.
newsitem.headline: China job market seen facing growing pressure.

text.p: China's job market will face increased pressure as more farmers shift to non-agricultural work and urban enterprises attempt to trim payrolls, a senior official said on Wednesday.
About 130 million farmers will likely move out of the agricultural sector in the next five years, vice-minister of labour Zhu Jiazhen told a business conference.
Millions of rural labourers have flooded China's cities in recent years in search of jobs created in the rush to a market economy.
More than 14 million people in urban areas would be seeking work after being laid off from companies that would shed workers as part of efforts to streamline state-run industries, Zhu said.
China has said it must reform its ailing state sector, which is overstaffed and losing money.
"The problem of an excessive supply of labour and the overall low quality of these labourers can hardly be solved within a short period of time," Zhu said in the report.
"There will be mounting pressure on the job market," he said.
Beijing would heighten efforts to train unskilled workers and improve unemployment insurance, Zhu said without giving further details.
China's official urban jobless rate is about 2.9 percent but the official media have warned that the actual figure could jump to 7.4 percent by the year 2000.
